newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Israel trying to undermine peace deals.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Israel trying to undermine peace deals.

text.p: Yasser Arafat, marking the eighth anniversary of the Palestinian declaration of independence, accused Israel on Saturday of pursuing a policy of "extremism and delays" to undermine existing peace agreements.

Six weeks of Israeli-PLO talks over a long-delayed Israeli troop pullout from most of the West Bank city of Hebron have produced no agreement. Other Israeli-Palestinian peace talks have been frozen since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in June.

"The Israeli government is trying to deny the whole peace process, and tries to destroy it through its policy of extremism and delays which it practices in an attempt to abandon accords signed in Cairo, Washington and in Taba," he said.

In the West Bank and Gaza Strip, Palestinians celebrated for the third consecutive day the statehood declaration made by Palestinian President Arafat in Algiers on November 15, 1988. The state won recognition by more than 100 countries.
"Concerning redeployment from Hebron, Israel's government is facing us with its intransigence and delaying tactics," Arafat said in a speech broadcast by Palestinian Radio and Television.
"In the beginning, they tried to renegotiate the whole issue, but we flatly rejected that on the basis that it constitutes a setback to the agreements and a dangerous, unacceptable precedent."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to alter the accord signed by the previous Labour government. He demands more safeguards for 400 militant Jewish settlers in heavily guarded enclaves in the middle of Hebron's 100,000 Arab residents.

Arafat said Netanyahu's policies were endangering the entire peace process. The Israeli leader rejects the exchange of occupied Arab land for peace -- a basic principle of the five years of peace talks -- and rules out Palestinian statehood.
Arafat wants the Hebron pact implemented as signed but said he was willing to discuss implementation of the accord.

"We accepted to discuss some practical security details which would secure redeployment in a better way, but every time we reached good results that would start the process, they backtracked and pushed things back to square one," he said.
Arafat embarked on the path of peace with Israel to achieve the Palestinians' goal of a state in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.

Netanyahu has taken pains to oppose signs of Palestinian sovereignty, especially in East Jerusalem. In a move largely unrecognised by the world community, Israel annexed the city's Arab half after capturing it in the 1967 Middle East war.

"The Declaration of Independence was not a radio statement, it was the first step and the first foothold over the beloved soil of our homeland, over our beloved Palestine, with Jerusalem as the capital of the Palestinian state, and that's the way it is whether they (Israelis) like it or not,"

The night skies of the West Bank and Gaza Strip were lit by fireworks and thousands of Palestinians flocked to events marking independence. On Saturday PLO-led troops and police paraded in such gathering points as Bethlehem's Manger Square.

The landmark 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal offered Palestinians self-rule for a five-year interim period. Under it, Israel handed over six major West Bank cities to the PLO but the withdrawal from Hebron was delayed because of a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in Israel early this year.
Talks on the ultimate fate of the Palestinian territories, including Jerusalem, have yet to resume under Netanyahu's right-wing government.
